title: Higher direct image sections vanishing on a principal open are power torsion
statement: Let f : X → T be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], F a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent], q a natural number and W an affine open of T. Let M = R^q f_* F [pqf-def-cohomology], a ∈ Γ(T,W), and let r be the restriction from W to the principal open D(a). For every t ∈ Γ(M,W) with r(t)=0, there is n ≥ 0 with a^n t=0.

source.place: Lemma 30.17.3, tensor-unit specialization, combined with Tag 01E4 and the localization criterion for quasi-coherence used in Tag 01XJ (1).

proof.text: Choose the standard injective resolution I of F and form P=H^q(f_*I) as presheaf homology. Its affine principal restrictions are module localizations.

The localization criterion makes the canonical sheafification unit an isomorphism on every affine open. Compose it with sectionCohomologyComparison and the inverse resolution comparison into R^q f_*F; the latter composite is an isomorphism by higherDirectImagePresheaf. Evaluation preserves this isomorphism. The resulting theta is a module-presheaf morphism with invertible components on W and D(a).

Lift t uniquely to x in P(W). Naturality of theta, its injectivity on D(a), and ht imply res(x)=0. Mathlib IsLocalizedModule.eq_zero_iff yields a power a^n killing x. Apply the linear component theta_W and its equality theta_W(x)=t to obtain a^n t=0.

proof_origin.place: Tensor-unit localization and extension from the principal-open basis, as in the original item plan.
